Afraid
uh-FRAYD
adj.
Participle of affray: Old French esfreer, to frighten. Webster 1828: impressed with fear or apprehension; fearful; a lesser degree than terrified or frightened; followed by of before the object. The KJV uses it for guilt in the garden, for the saint who trusts while he is still afraid, and for the Lord’s command, be not afraid, when His presence is the reason.

Biblical Definition

Afraid in Scripture is not a mood to be managed. It is the creature answering a presence. Adam’s first word after the fall is this: I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself (Gen 3:10). That fear is guilt before the Holy, not a chemical event. David does not pretend the feeling is gone; he relocates it: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee (Ps 56:3). Isaiah names the ground that ends it: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid (Isa 12:2). The LORD is light and strength, of whom shall I be afraid? (Ps 27:1). In the boat the object is a Person: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid (Matt 14:27). The dictionary therefore keeps two fears from collapsing. The fear of the LORD is worship. Being afraid of nakedness, of men, of the night, of death, is the heart still measuring the wrong presence. The gospel does not scold the pulse into silence. It puts Jehovah in the place of the threat, and then says be not afraid because it is I.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines AFRAID as impressed with fear or apprehension; fearful. It expresses a less degree of fear than terrified or frightened, and is followed by of before the object of fear.

expand to see more

AFRAID, a. [The participle of affray.] — Impressed with fear or apprehension; fearful. This word expresses a less degree of fear than terrified or frightened. It is followed by of before the object of fear; as, to be afraid of death.

Webster’s own illustration is moral, not theatrical: Joseph was afraid to sin against God.

Key Scripture

Genesis 3:10 — "And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself."

Psalm 56:3 — "What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee."

Isaiah 12:2 — "Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid: for the LORD JEHOVAH is my strength and my song; he also is become my salvation."

Psalm 27:1 — "A Psalm of David. The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?"

Matthew 14:27 — "But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid."

Modern Corruption

Afraid is corrupted when guilt before God is recast as a wellness problem, when stoic self-help pretends the saint need never feel it, and when “be not afraid” is sold as a vibe with the Speaker left out.

expand to see more

The first corruption is to medicalize Adam. Genesis 3:10 is nakedness and hiding, not a diagnosis. Wellness culture treats every fear as a symptom to soothe, and so it cannot hear the Lord’s voice in the garden. The recovery is confession: the first fear after the fall is guilt, and hiding is not healing.

The second corruption is Stoic and athletic courage that scolds the saint for still being afraid. Psalm 56:3 will not play that game. David is afraid, and in that hour he trusts. Christian manhood is not the absence of the pulse. It is trust while the pulse is still running. The fear of the LORD remains; being afraid of men is what faith dethrones.

The third corruption is to empty Matthew 14:27. Progressive unbelief and inspirational religion both like the slogan and drop the clause that carries it: it is I. Courage without Christ is still the boat in the dark. The Lord does not send a technique across the water. He sends Himself, and then He forbids fear.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

English participle of affray (Old French esfreer). Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Hebrew yārē’ (H3372) at Ps 56:3; Hebrew pāḥad (H6342) at Isa 12:2 and Ps 27:1; Greek phobeō (G5399) at Matt 14:27. Genesis 3:10 is untagged in this cache; no Hebrew number is invented for it. The companion entry fear already treats the fear of the LORD as worship; this page is the English adjective afraid.

expand to see more

Hebrew yārē’ (H3372) — to fear, to revere (Ps 56:3, What time I am afraid).

Hebrew pāḥad (H6342) — to tremble, to be in dread (Isa 12:2; Ps 27:1, of whom shall I be afraid).

Greek phobeō (G5399) — to fear, to be afraid (Matt 14:27, be not afraid).

Genesis 3:10 untagged in this cache — no Hebrew number is minted for Adam’s I was afraid.

Usage

"Adam was afraid because he was naked — the first fear after the fall is guilt, not weather."

"David is still afraid when he trusts (Ps 56:3); faith does not wait for the pulse to stop."

"Be not afraid stands on it is I (Matt 14:27), not on a technique."
